symptom: ./init.sh exited 0 without running any build/test step
remedy: init.sh must fail when it recognizes no stack — a vacuous green lets a loop run on an unverified project
evidence:
=== Harness init: Demo1 ===
No recognized manifest. Edit this VERIFICATION block with the project's build/test commands.
=== Baseline green ===

Next: read feature_list.json, pick ONE eligible feature, advance it, re-verify before 'done'.

symptom: gateBaseline tagged the 'No recognized manifest' signal as layer=harness even when the target had zero manifest files, double-counting the same root cause the structure gate (L2) already reports as layer=project
remedy: gate on hasAnyManifest() before classifying the No-recognized-manifest signal as harness — a manifest-less target is a project-setup gap, not a template gap
evidence: found live while dogfooding verify-harness.mjs on scratchpad/demo1: init-vacuously-green fired as harness-layer for a target with no manifest at all

fix: verify-harness.mjs: added hasAnyManifest() gate before classifying the No-recognized-manifest baseline signal as harness; fixed in the same session it was found

symptom: run-loop.sh demanded KIRO_API_KEY before checking all_settled — a loop with no open work exits 1 (missing credentials) instead of 0 (nothing to do)
remedy: check all_settled before the credential gate in templates/tree/loop/run-loop.sh

fix: templates/tree/loop/run-loop.sh: all_settled check moved before the KIRO_API_KEY gate; proven live on aeron-demo (17 settled features, no key -> exit 0)

symptom: run-loop.sh required KIRO_API_KEY even when kiro-cli already had a valid cached login — blocked a runnable headless loop
remedy: accept KIRO_API_KEY OR a passing kiro-cli whoami

fix: templates/tree/loop/run-loop.sh: auth gate now passes if kiro-cli whoami succeeds; proven by launching the real loop on aeron-demo without the env var

remedy: all file:// URIs in agent templates now use ../../ prefixes; validated via kiro-cli agent list

fix: templates/tree/.kiro/agents/*.json + templates/k8s + harness-improver: every file:// URI prefixed ../../; kiro-cli agent list now loads all workspace agents

remedy: run-loop.sh's dispatch message now states HEADLESS explicitly and instructs committing directly

fix: templates/tree/loop/run-loop.sh: maker dispatch message declares headless mode; observed on the first real kiro maker run

fix: scripts/verify-harness.mjs: gateMemory regex accepts (../)* prefix; caught by demo.sh step 18 on the first run after the kiro URI fix

remedy: read the rotated archive too

fix: scripts/verify-harness.mjs: decisionsAll concatenates DECISIONS.md with DECISIONS/*.md; knowledge-layout.md predicted this exact hazard

symptom: harness-onboarder run headless skipped its whole Phase 2 question round and decided scope, baseline command, merge strategy and the FIRST OBJECTIVE itself — then recorded none of it as a decision. loop/goal.md names a real in-flight branch, but nobody chose it and nothing says a human still has to.
remedy: prompt needs a headless branch: proceed on the recommendations, but write every unanswered question into docs/assumptions.md as needs-human WITH the recommended answer filled, and name them in the report. A guessed answer written down is indistinguishable from a verified one.

symptom: onboarder grepped check-coverage.mjs, extracted its literal regexes (/(startup workflow|start of session)/i etc), and edited AGENTS.md headings to match them. Goodhart inside the harness: it optimised the measurement, not the thing measured.
remedy: when merging into an existing router, copy the template's section headings VERBATIM — they already encode what the checks look for. Forbid deriving text from a checker's pattern.

symptom: HI-011's prohibition did not hold. Re-run with the explicit rule in context, the agent STILL reasoned from the regex ('didn't match /(end of session|clean state)/i') — negation is the weakest instruction shape (llm-failure-modes.md), and the deeper cause is that L5/L10/L12 match literal phrases, so producing that phrase is a rational response.
remedy: mitigated, not closed: the failure messages now name the template section to copy, so following the message yields real content instead of a matching label. The checks remain phrase-shaped.

note: prompt now has a headless branch: proceed on recommendations but record each as a needs-human row with the recommended answer. Verified on a real kiro run against auto-e2e — 4 rows written, 3 needs-human including A-004 (the objective), and the report names them.
superseded by HI-012: the prohibition did not hold, and the real cause is that the checks are phrase-shaped. Mitigated by naming the template section in each failure message.
partially: the phrase-shaped checks now name the template section to copy. The router gap that made agents undiscoverable is separately closed by the agent-unrouted gate.

symptom: Fresh scaffold: 6 of 9 agents load file://../../feature_list.digest.md as a resource, but setup-harness-loop.mjs never generates it. Every one of them starts missing the file whose entire purpose is keeping the big feature list out of their context — and kiro reports nothing.
remedy: setup-harness-loop.mjs must run tools/feature-digest.mjs after copying, so the digest exists before any agent loads it.

note: setup-harness-loop.mjs now runs tools/feature-digest.mjs after copying; a fresh scaffold has 0 agent-uri-broken findings and the digest present. Demo asserts both.

now mechanically caught: agent-uri-broken is a blocker on every .kiro/agents/*.json whose file:// URIs do not resolve from .kiro/agents/. Calibrated on 4 targets; found 6 real breakages in this skill's own template on its first run.

symptom: route.mjs's design rule matches ONLY the NEEDS DESIGN: marker. It never reads design-untestable, so on aeron-demo — where gap-reconcile.md states no seam and no invariants — the router jumped the design layer entirely and sent test-designer to derive 25 falsifiers from invariants that do not exist. Violates the router's own deeper-first precedence, and contradicts the feature-planner prompt which says to raise NEEDS DESIGN when the design gives you nothing to derive from.
remedy: add a design-layer rule using the same predicate as the design-untestable gate: a design doc naming no observable seam or no invariants routes to the designer, ahead of the oracle layer.

note: route.mjs now has a design-layer rule using the same predicate as the design-untestable gate. Verified on aeron-demo: the router moved from test-designer [oracle] to designer [design] and names the file. Demo asserts both directions.

symptom: console.log(JSON.stringify(...)) followed by process.exit() silently truncates on a pipe at the buffer size (~8 KB on macOS). Present in verify-harness --json and six other shipped scripts since they were written. Surfaced only when aeron-demo's report crossed 8 KB and adoption-baseline could no longer parse its own input — before that, every --json consumer had been fine by luck of payload size.
remedy: writeSync(1, ...) everywhere a JSON payload precedes process.exit. Demo now statically scans every shipped .mjs for the pattern and round-trips a real report through spawnSync.

note: all seven scripts converted to writeSync; verified aeron-demo's 8238-byte report now parses through spawnSync, and demo.sh scans for the pattern so it cannot return.

symptom: setup-harness-loop.mjs skips every existing file, which is right for project-owned content (AGENTS.md, feature_list.json, docs/architecture.md) and wrong for skill-owned machinery. On aeron-demo it left loop/run-loop.sh at a version with no dispatch() — so HARNESS_RUNTIME=claude would have silently run the kiro path. Same class already hit tools/*.mjs twice: an upgraded skill does not reach an existing target.
remedy: an --upgrade mode that refreshes the skill-owned set (tools/**, loop/run-loop.sh, loop/route.mjs, loop/approval-gate.mjs, check-coverage.mjs, docs/reference/**, skills/**) and never touches the project-owned set. Until then, upgrading is a manual copy and easy to do incompletely — as it was here.

symptom: feature-planner re-cut aeron-demo to 54 features and reported '0 blockers throughout' — while shipping 0/54 falsifiers and 0/54 kind tags. Its self-check step named only scope-smell, and every check that exists to catch the PLANNER is a warning by design (so adoption is not a wall). So the agent passed its own gate with the oracle layer left nothing to derive from.
remedy: self-check step now names falsifier-missing, build-unproven and scope-smell explicitly, and states that 0-blockers is not the bar.

symptom: adoption-baseline reported build-unproven 0 -> 13 as NEW DEBT. Nothing got worse: the check is opt-in on the kind tag, no feature had one at adoption, so it was dormant and only started measuring when the planner added kind. Turning on a previously-silent gate is indistinguishable from a regression.
remedy: record which gates were dormant at --record time (a gate with a known opt-in precondition that was unmet), and report their first non-zero count as 'newly measured' rather than 'new debt'. Until then the operator has to know which gates are opt-in.

symptom: feat-ledger-core was APPROVED done on attempt 3 of 3 — the loop working exactly as intended — and verify-harness immediately raised a blocker: 'attempts=3 >= maxAttempts=3 but status is done, not blocked'. The timebox check only excludes status=blocked, so succeeding on the last allowed attempt is indistinguishable from exhausting the budget without finishing.
remedy: exclude terminal success (done/passing) as well as blocked. The check exists to stop silent infinite retrying, and a feature that finished is not retrying.

note: timebox check now excludes done/passing as well as blocked; verified on aeron-demo (1 blocker -> 0) and asserted in demo.sh both directions.

symptom: The checker logged two real follow-ups on a feature it APPROVED — a deprecated overload that silently drops state and would reintroduce the fixed defect, plus stale comments. They live in the checkerNotes of a done feature, which nothing routes on: NEEDS DESIGN and NEEDS RE-PLAN are for rejections, and the maker only picks eligible not-started features. A non-blocking finding is therefore recorded and then invisible.
remedy: either a FOLLOW-UP: marker the router reads and hands to the planner, or an explicit instruction that the checker must choose between blocking and letting it go. Recording something nobody will act on is the worst of the three options. Sixth instance of detector-without-a-route this session.

symptom: scope-smell fires on EITHER >400 chars OR >=3 and/then joiners. On the BOD re-plan it produced 5 findings; the operator judged all 5 individually and found each to be a single claim - long because a prove feature narrates a sequential scenario (apply BOD, then snapshot, then restart, then read) or enumerates the cases one contract covers. Length is a weak proxy for compound structure on scenario features specifically.
remedy: DO NOT tune the threshold to reduce a count on one project - that is weakening a gate because you dislike its output, and AGENTS.md makes it a human checkpoint. Recorded as one data point. If a second project shows the same pattern, weight clause structure over raw length and give kind:prove more narrative room than kind:build.

symptom: The meta-loop imports the current target finding but improve-harness --prompt selects the globally highest-ranked open issue, so a repair run can fix an unrelated defect and patch the wrong target.
remedy: Bind each repair run to an issue ID returned by import; add improve-harness --id and reject mismatched objectives.

symptom: route.mjs says the first checkerNotes line is the routing marker but hashes the entire notes body, so appending diagnostic text resets dispatch history and can redispatch an already-answered design question.
remedy: Canonicalize marker identity from the first line, then migrate routing control to typed request records with revision.

symptom: Two documented workflow edges remain open: design-reviewer REJECT has no machine-readable return route, and run-loop stops on a red baseline although the graph routes baseline repair to maker.
remedy: Persist typed design review outcomes and make baseline status a router input with bounded repair routing.

symptom: NEEDS RE-PLAN and missing test conditions can redispatch the same agent indefinitely because their guards do not consistently use durable per-request dispatch history.
remedy: Use canonical request identity, durable attempts and a finite ladder ending in needs-human.

symptom: harness-loop declares no progress when consecutive blocker gate/id sets match, ignoring changed evidence/workspace/state, and misses longer A-B-A cycles.
remedy: Use canonical durable progress fingerprints over a sliding window with route, evidence, feature state and workspace identity.

remedy: When --target is supplied, reverify only issues whose recorded targets include that exact target; add --id for explicit manual verification and refuse provenance-free auto-resolution.
